title: Azizam documentation
summary: Install a gateway, connect your apps, and give each person their own access.
text: Azizam is an AI gateway that you run on a computer you control. It puts the engines you run, and any paid providers you choose, behind one OpenAI-compatible address. Each person and each app gets its own key and access plan. Choose where to start · Run a gatewayInstall Azizam, connect an engine and get a first reply. Use a gatewaySomeone invited you. Use Try, Library, Apps & keys and Usage. Build with the APIConnect an app, an SDK or an agent with your app key. What Azizam does · The gateway sits between your apps and the engines that do the model work. An app sends a request with its app key. The gateway checks the key and the app's access plan. The gateway sends the request to the engine or provider that serves the chosen model. The gateway records a receipt for the request, on routes that record receipts. You choose the engines. Engine addresses and model names are settings, not code. You can replace an engine without changing the gateway. What you need to bring · A computer to run the gateway, with Docker and Docker Compose. At least one engine that serves an OpenAI-compatible chat API, with a model already loaded. Model files for any image, video or audio work you want to do. Azizam does not download or install models. What you can do depends on the engines and model files you connect. Before you rely on it · A route that accepts a vendor's API format does not mean that every feature of that API works. Each page under Build with the API lists its limits. A local model that is down does not silently become a paid request. Paid providers need explicit setup and permission. See Providers and spend. You run the computer. Updates, backups and HTTPS for other devices are your responsibility. See Upgrade and back up and Security. Find your way around · Section Use it to Start here Install a gateway and get a first reply. Use a gateway Do everyday tasks as a member. Run a gateway Connect engines, invite people, keep the gateway safe and up to date. Build with the API Connect apps, SDKs and agents. Concepts Understand how access, keys, receipts and privacy work. Reference Look up settings, error codes and terms. Use Search at the top of any page, or press /.

title: Install Azizam
summary: Start the gateway with Docker Compose and connect it to an engine on the same computer.

headings.text: Connect to an engine on the same computer

text: This page installs the gateway with Docker Compose on one computer. At the end, the gateway runs on that computer and its setup page opens in a browser. Before you start · You need: Docker with a Compose plugin that supports optional env_file entries (required: false). A copy of the Azizam repository. Network access to download container images and build dependencies. An engine that serves an OpenAI-compatible chat API, with a model loaded. You connect it in First run. Compose starts two containers: the gateway and its execution sidecar. Neither one downloads a model. Start the gateway · Open a terminal in the root of the repository and run: ShellCopy docker compose up -d docker compose ps The first build takes the longest. It installs the web dependencies and builds the browser interface. When the gateway is running, open this address in a browser on the same computer: TextCopy http://127.0.0.1:5000/setup You do not need a .env file for a local engine that does not require credentials. For a host-based engine or one that requires a key, complete the connection setup below before continuing with First run. The gateway health check probes /health; a running or healthy gateway does not prove that an engine can answer. The litellm sidecar waits for /app/data/litellm.config.yaml before starting its server, so a running sidecar container alone is not a readiness check. Finish engine setup and send the real request in First run. Use a different port · The gateway publishes port 5000 on the computer's loopback address only. Other devices cannot reach it yet. See Security before you open it to other devices. To use another port, set AZIZAM_PORT when you start Compose. This example uses 5001: ShellCopy AZIZAM_PORT=5001 docker compose up -d Then open http://127.0.0.1:5001/setup. Use the same setting every time you run a Compose command that recreates the gateway. Connect to an engine on the same computer · The gateway and execution sidecar run in separate containers, so 127.0.0.1 inside either container is that container itself, not your computer. Both need to reach the engine. The supplied Compose file adds host.docker.internal only to the gateway; add the same alias to the sidecar instead of relying on Docker to provide it automatically. Create compose.override.yaml beside docker-compose.yml with the following content, or merge this service setting into an existing override: YAMLCopy services: litellm: extra_hosts: - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway" Apply it from the repository root: ShellCopy docker compose up -d Compose automatically reads this override alongside docker-compose.yml. Preserve your AZIZAM_PORT and network settings when recreating containers. For example, an engine that listens on port 8080 of your computer has this address: TextCopy http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1 An engine that listens only on the computer's loopback address is not reachable from the container. Make the engine listen on an address the container can reach, and use your firewall to restrict who else can reach it. If the Compose network conflicts with another network on your computer, set AZIZAM_DOCKER_SUBNET and AZIZAM_DOCKER_GATEWAY together. See Configuration. Configure engine credentials · Skip this section if your engine does not require a key. Otherwise, choose an environment variable name, such as MY_ENGINE_API_KEY, and put its value in the repository's local .env file. Keep that file private; do not commit it or paste the value into the browser's Key environment variable field. The supplied Compose file loads .env into the gateway, but not into the litellm sidecar. Pass the engine credential to the sidecar too. Add this setting under services.litellm in compose.override.yaml, alongside extra_hosts if you added it above: YAMLCopy services: litellm: environment: MY_ENGINE_API_KEY: ${MY_ENGINE_API_KEY:?Set MY_ENGINE_API_KEY in .env} Use your chosen variable name in both places. This forwards only that variable to the sidecar rather than every value in .env. Then recreate the containers so both processes receive the new environment: ShellCopy docker compose up -d In First run, enter MY_ENGINE_API_KEY (the name, not its value) as the engine's key environment variable. Repeat the recreation after changing its value. AZIZAM_LITELLM_API_KEY is the gateway-to-sidecar credential; it is not your engine provider key. Where your data lives · Data Where Kept when you replace the container Accounts, apps, keys, settings and receipts Named volume gateway-data, at /app/data Yes Creations (pictures, audio, video) and the key that signs download links Named volume gateway-cache, at /app/cache Yes Keep both volumes when you rebuild or replace containers. docker compose up -d --build keeps them. docker compose down --volumes deletes them, and so does docker volume rm. If you installed an earlier version that kept creations inside the container, download the creations you want to keep before your first upgrade. They are not in the new volume. Read Upgrade and back up before you replace an installation. Next step · First run: create the owner account, connect your engine and get a first reply.

title: First run
summary: Create the owner account, connect a chat engine, and get a first reply in your app.

headings.text: Send the same request with curl

text: This tutorial takes a new gateway to its first reply. You create the owner account, connect one chat engine, create an app key and send a message. Before you start, install Azizam and make sure your chat engine is running with a model loaded. The examples below use the default port, 5000. If you changed AZIZAM_PORT during installation, replace 5000 in every URL on this page with that port. Run curl on the gateway computer. The app URL also assumes the app runs directly on that computer. For an app on another device or in another container, first configure a reachable gateway address using the Security guide. 1. Create the owner account · On the computer that runs the gateway, open: TextCopy http://127.0.0.1:5000/setup Create the owner account. The owner can configure the gateway and invite other people. 2. Connect your engine · Open Engines, in the Gateway group of the menu, and select Add engine. Enter a name and your engine's OpenAI-compatible base URL. Use an http:// address that the gateway can reach. For an engine on the same computer, see Connect to an engine on the same computer. If the engine needs a key, first configure engine credentials for both the gateway and execution sidecar. Enter that variable's name in Key environment variable. Do not paste the key itself. Select Test connection, then add the engine. On the engine, select Detect models to read the engine's models. Map the model name apps will send to the engine's actual model ID. For example, map the public name my-chat to the exact ID returned by your engine; do not substitute my-chat for that ID unless it really is the engine's ID. This tutorial uses my-chat as the model name. It is an example, not a built-in model. Use your own name in the steps below if you chose a different one. Check the engine's health settings as well. For an OpenAI-compatible engine, a models endpoint such as http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1/models can provide positive health evidence when it returns a non-empty model list. Use your engine's real address and port, and avoid adding /v1 twice. An unknown health status is not a successful connection; see Read health status. A real chat reply is still the end-to-end test. The engine and its model names are settings. You can change or replace them later without changing the gateway. 3. Create an app key · Open Home. Choose the app you want to connect, then select Create key for that app. Save the key when it appears. It is shown only once. Use app keys in apps. Do not put an admin key in an app. 4. Get a first reply · In your app, use these settings: Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:5000/openai/v1 API key: the app key you saved Model: my-chat Send a short message from your app, or use the curl request below. A reply means that the app key, gateway, model mapping and engine work together; a gateway health check alone does not establish this. Send the same request with curl · Run this example in Bash on the gateway computer. If your terminal uses another shell, run bash first. It reads the key without echoing it and asks for a streamed reply. Your curl must support --fail-with-body. Copy read -r -s -p 'App key: ' AZIZAM_API_KEY && printf '\n' && curl --no-buffer --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ http://127.0.0.1:5000/openai/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"model":"my-chat","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}]}' unset AZIZAM_API_KEY The reply arrives as a stream of events. The text is in choices[0].delta.content. The stream ends with data: [DONE]. If there is no reply · The request is refused. Check that you used an app key, not an admin key, and that you copied all of it. The model is not found. Open Models to see the model names your key can use. The engine is busy or starting. Check Status, then try again. See Troubleshooting for error codes. Next steps · Invite people to use your gateway. Connect more engines for images, video or audio. Before other devices connect, read Security. Before you upgrade, read Upgrade and back up.

title: Use a gateway
summary: Everyday tasks for people who use a gateway that someone else runs.
text: This section is for members: people who use a gateway that someone else runs. The person who runs it is the owner. Sign in · Open the gateway address that the owner gave you. If the page says Sign in to connect your apps, select Sign in. Choose what to do · Page Use it to Try Send a message, make a picture, hear text spoken aloud, or turn a recording into text. See Try. Library Find the pictures, videos and audio you made. See Library. Apps & keys Connect an app you already use. See Apps & keys. Usage Check this month's requests and open receipts. See Usage and receipts. What you can use depends on the engines the owner connected and on your access plan. If a model or task is missing, ask the owner. What the owner can see · The owner can see your creations and your request activity. Your saved prompts are shown only to you in Library. Read Privacy and the owner for the details and the limits.

title: Try
summary: Send a message, make a picture, make speech, or turn audio into text in the browser.

headings.text: Choose a task and a model

text: Use Try to run a single request in the browser. Each task shows the request it sends, so you can repeat it from your own app later. Choose a task and a model · Open Try and select the task you want. On a phone, swipe the row of tasks to see more. Open Model name and choose a model. Read any availability message before you run the task. Some models show a paid label. A paid model sends your request to an outside provider. Send a message · Choose the chat task. Enter your message in Prompt. Select Run. The reply appears in the result area. Each run sends only the message in the box. Earlier replies are not sent as conversation history. Make a picture · Choose the picture task and a model. Describe the picture in Prompt. Select Run. While the picture is made, Try says that you can switch to another app and it keeps going. To start from a picture you already have, for example to edit or upscale it, look under Workflow. Make speech · Choose the speech task and a model. Enter the words in Prompt. Choose a voice, if the model offers a choice. Select Run. Play the result in the audio player, or use the download link when one is shown. Turn audio into text · Choose the transcription task and a model. Select an Audio file, or select Record. Select Stop when you finish recording. Select Run. The text appears in the result area. If recording does not start, check that the browser can use the microphone, or choose a file. Run a workflow · A workflow is a named task, such as making a video or a piece of music. The gateway lists only the workflows the owner set up. Choose Workflow, then choose a workflow under Model name. Fill in the fields it shows, and add any files it asks for. Select Run. If a required input is missing, the form points to it. If the result shows Check job, select it to check for the output. When the output is ready, use the player or the download link. Don't keep a prompt · Before you make a picture, speech or a workflow result, look above Run for Don’t keep this prompt. Turn it on when you do not want the prompt kept with the creation. The creation still goes to Library. The result can show Prompt not kept. Try remembers the switch for this browser session, when the browser allows it. Check it before later runs. Picture and workflow jobs with a prompt that is not kept cannot resume after a gateway restart. If prompt keeping is already off, the row says Prompts aren’t kept instead. If you turned it off yourself, Change opens Your settings. If the owner turned it off for everyone, the row says so. Read Prompt saving to learn what is kept and for how long.

title: Library
summary: Find, open, download and delete the pictures, videos and audio you made.
text: Library holds the pictures, videos and audio you made. Find a creation · Open Library. Enter text in Search your creations. On a phone, select the search icon first. Choose All, Images, Video or Audio to narrow the list. Select Filters to choose a Model or a Date: Any time, Last 7 days, Last 30 days or Last 90 days. If nothing matches, select Clear filters. A creation without a saved prompt is named by its type and time. Open a creation · Select a creation to open it. Use Previous creation and Next creation to move through the list, and Close to return. When a saved prompt is available, you can read it and select Copy prompt. When a receipt link is shown, select it to open the receipt for the request. Download a creation · Open the creation. Select Download, and wait while the file is prepared. Some creations also offer Download with details in the actions menu. That file includes the prompt and the workflow text. Think about who will see it before you pass it on. A downloaded copy cannot be recalled. Delete a creation · Open the creation, then open its actions menu. Select Delete, if it is shown. Read the confirmation, then select Delete. This removes the creation from your Library. Copies you downloaded stay where they are. See Library and retention for what deletion does on the gateway. When a file is unavailable · Library lists unavailable files separately. Select Show them to see these items, and Refresh library to check again. The message distinguishes files that are unavailable from files that are no longer stored. An unavailable creation can still have a receipt.

title: Apps & keys
summary: Connect a chat app or agent, and create, rotate or revoke its keys.

headings.text: Connect a chat app or agent
Create a key for an existing app
When you cannot create a key

text: Give each app its own key. Then you can stop one app without breaking the others. Connect a chat app or agent · Open Apps & keys and select New app. Enter an App name and choose an App recipe. Choose Other app if yours is not listed. Select Create app and key. Save the key while it is shown. You cannot see it again. In your app, choose its OpenAI-compatible provider setting. Paste the gateway address that Azizam shows, and enter the key. Use Connection examples if you need a setup example. If a prompt-saving note is shown with the key, read it. See Client setup examples for common apps. Create a key for an existing app · Find the app in the list. Select Create key, or open the app's actions menu and select Create key or Create another key. Save the key before you leave the screen. If the app was created but its key was not, select Retry key creation. Rotate keys · Rotate keys when a key may have leaked, or to replace old keys on a schedule. Open the app's actions menu and select Rotate keys. Select Create replacement key, and save the new key. Update your app to use the new key. Confirm that you saved the key. This starts to revoke the old keys. If some old keys still work, select Retry revoking old keys. You can also select Finish later. The app then shows Revoke old keys while the old keys are active. If the browser says it could not save that reminder, revoke the old keys before you leave the page. Stop an app from connecting · Open the app's actions menu. Revoke keys revokes the app's keys. The app stops connecting. Remove app removes the app and its keys. Each action asks you to confirm. When you cannot create a key · Read the message shown for the app. The app may be turned off, or its access plan may have been removed. Ask the owner to check the app's access. Read Apps and keys to learn what a key can do, including access to your saved prompts.

title: Usage and receipts
summary: Check this month's requests and spend, and open the receipt for a request.
text: Usage shows this month's requests, spend, creations and failures. Check this month · Open Usage. The tiles show Requests, Spend, Media made and Failed. The daily and model sections give more detail when records are available. Cost not recorded means that the amount is unknown. It does not mean that the request was free. No provider charge on a receipt means that its record says the request stayed on the gateway's own engines. Open a receipt · A receipt shows what happened to one request: its task, model, source, time, duration and outcome, when they were recorded. Select View recent requests. Select a request to open its receipt. You can also open a receipt from Try or Library when a receipt link is shown. Check coverage · Open Receipt coverage, when it is shown, to read how much history the totals include. The totals may not include every past request. When usage does not load · Select Retry usage. Until a refresh succeeds, the totals on screen are the last ones that loaded. Couldn’t open this receipt means the receipt did not load. Select Try again. Receipt not available means the receipt may belong to someone else or may have been deleted. Select Dismiss to close the message. Read Receipts and usage to learn how the totals are counted.

title: When something fails
summary: What to do when a list, a request, a recording, a download or a key change fails.

headings.text: The model or workflow list does not load
The connection drops while something is made

text: Read the message on screen first. It names the problem and, in most cases, the next step. The model or workflow list does not load · Select Retry model catalog or Retry workflow catalog. If the page says that no options are listed, nothing is available for that choice. Ask the owner. A request fails · Read the message in Try. Select Edit and run again when it is offered. Your values stay in the form. Check them, then select Run. The button does not repeat the request on its own. The connection drops while something is made · The gateway may still be making it. Select Open Library when it is offered, and look for the finished creation before you start another run. For other requests, reconnect and use Edit and run again. A workflow is still running · Select Check job when it is shown. This checks for the output of the job that is already running. Recording fails · Check that the browser can use the microphone. Then select Record again, or choose an Audio file. A download fails · Select Download again. If Library could not prepare the file, open the creation and try again. A key change fails · If the app exists but its key was not created, select Retry key creation. If a replacement key is saved but the old keys still work, retry revoking them. Rotation is not finished while that warning is shown. Usage does not refresh · Select Retry usage. Until it succeeds, the totals on screen are old. If a problem continues, tell the owner what you did and what the message said. Do not send your key, a download link or private media.

title: Connect engines
summary: Add an engine, map model names, and read its health status correctly.
text: An engine is a server that does model work: chat, pictures, speech or video. The gateway keeps a record for each engine. The record holds its address, its model names, its health probe and any changes the gateway makes to requests for it. These records are settings. Use the values for the engines you actually run. No engine or model name in these docs is required. Add an engine · Open Engines, in the Gateway group of the menu, and select Add engine. Choose a preset if one fits, then enter a name and the engine's base URL. The address must use http:// and be reachable from the gateway. In Docker Compose, see Connect to an engine on the same computer. If the engine needs a key, put the key in an environment variable of the gateway, and enter the variable's name in Key environment variable. In Docker Compose, add the variable to the .env file in the repository, then run docker compose up -d again. Select Test connection, then add the engine. Select Detect models, and map each model name that apps will use to the engine's own model ID. Then check the engine's status and send a real request, for example from Try, before you tell other people to use it. Change an engine safely · Save a copy of the current settings before you change them. Change one engine at a time. After the change, check both its status and a real request. The gateway applies a saved change without a restart. Read health status · A health probe can report one of three things: healthy, not healthy, or unknown. Unknown does not mean healthy. An engine record can declare positive health evidence: health_endpoint: the address the gateway probes. health_success_path: a dot-separated path into the probe's JSON response. For example, if a probe response contains a system object, set health_success_path to system. A 2xx response whose selected value is not null and not false counts as healthy. Explicit failure, starting and busy states take precedence. Without a success path, a 2xx JSON response counts as healthy only when it says so in a common form: a non-empty model list, a status of ok, up, healthy or ready, or a true ready, available, ok or healthy field. Any other response stays unknown. That is why /v1/models works for an OpenAI-compatible engine. Change request and response shapes · Some engines need small changes to requests, such as a renamed or dropped parameter. Put these in the engine record as data, not in the gateway's code. Before you change one, save an example request and response with secrets removed. After the change, compare the new request, response and errors. Test with the value left out as well as with it set. A healthy probe does not prove that the request is right. Read Engines and models for how engines, models and workflows fit together, and Troubleshooting when an engine is reachable but requests fail.

title: Invite people
summary: Create an access plan, send an invitation link, and give each person their own key.
text: Each person you invite gets their own account, their own app and their own key. Their access plan sets what they can use. Before you invite anyone · Choose an access plan. The plan decides which models and workflows a person can use. Read Access plans. Make the gateway reachable. A person on another device cannot use 127.0.0.1: that address points to their own device. Set up an HTTPS address and secure cookies first. See Open the gateway to other devices. Send an invitation · Open People, in the Gateway group of the menu. Create an invite. Choose the access plan and when the invite expires. The default is 7 days; the range is one minute to 30 days. Copy the invitation link, and send it to the person yourself. The gateway does not send email. What the person does · When the person accepts the invitation, the gateway creates an account and a personal app called My first app for them, and shows the app's key once. They then follow Use a gateway and connect their apps with Apps & keys.

title: Security
summary: Control who can set up the gateway, protect keys, and open it safely to other devices.

headings.text: Who can create the owner account
Open the gateway to other devices
What the gateway sends to engines

text: Keep access closed until you have decided who may use the gateway. A reachable page, a home network address or a healthy engine is not permission to run requests. Who can create the owner account · Setup creates the owner account. It works only while the gateway has no owner or admin, and only from allowed networks: Loopback is always allowed. AZIZAM_SETUP_ALLOWED_CIDRS lists more networks. It overrides auth.setup_allowed_cidrs in the configuration file. If neither is set, setup uses auth.lan_bypass_cidrs. In Docker Compose, setup is allowed only from the computer that runs the containers. Compose sets AZIZAM_SETUP_ALLOWED_CIDRS itself. Setup permission does not allow anyone to run requests without a key. Keys · App keys run requests. Give each app its own key, so you can revoke one without breaking the others. Admin keys change the gateway's configuration. Keep them out of apps. Protect every key as you would a password. Do not put keys in URLs, screenshots, shared logs or support reports. Open the gateway to other devices · The default installation listens only on the computer's loopback address. Before other devices connect: Put HTTPS in front of the gateway, for example with a reverse proxy. Turn on secure cookies: in the configuration file, set admin.oidc.cookie.secure to true. In Docker Compose, the configuration file is first-run.yml in the repository, and the change needs a rebuild with docker compose up -d --build. Keep the gateway's own port and your engines' ports closed to the outside. Test access through the public address, not only through loopback. A healthy local check does not prove that the reverse proxy reaches the gateway. What the gateway sends to engines · The gateway forwards only Content-Type, Accept and User-Agent from the client, with Accept-Encoding: identity. It does not forward gateway cookies, CSRF tokens, internal headers or credentials in query parameters. To authenticate the gateway to an engine, put the engine's key in an environment variable of the gateway, and enter the variable's name in Key environment variable for that engine. Do not write keys into the configuration file. Fetching media from URLs · When a request gives a media URL, the gateway fetches it with limits. It does not fetch from private network addresses unless you list the exact host in AZIZAM_MEDIA_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS. Even then, it does not fetch from loopback, link-local or cloud metadata addresses. See Configuration. Single sign-on button label · In Settings → Sign-in, the owner can set the name of the identity provider. It appears on the sign-in button. A saved value takes precedence over AZIZAM_ADMIN_OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME. An empty value shows the generic single sign-on label. The name can have up to 80 characters, with no angle brackets or control characters. Check that denial works · Before you open the gateway to other people: Send a request without a key, and check that it is refused. Sign in as a member, and check that they see only their own work. Report a problem safely · When you report a failure, include the error code, the message and the layer. Remove keys, cookies, private addresses, prompts and personal data first.

title: Upgrade and back up
summary: Back up the gateway's state, upgrade it, restart it safely, and check the result.

headings.text: Restart a gateway that runs as a systemd service

text: Treat an upgrade as maintenance. Make a backup first, and write down the version you are replacing. What to back up · The data volume. In Docker Compose, accounts, apps, keys, settings and receipts are in the gateway-data volume, mounted at /app/data. The gateway and the execution sidecar both use it. The cache volume. Creations and the key that signs download links are in the gateway-cache volume, mounted at /app/cache. Rebuilding the container keeps them. If you lose the key, old download links stop working. Your start-up settings. Keep your Compose changes, first-run.yml changes and your .env file, if you use one. Store backups privately. A container image is not a backup of its data. To copy both volumes while the containers are stopped, run these commands from the root of the repository. Compose adds the project name to volume names, so find the exact names with docker volume ls. This example assumes the project name azizam: ShellCopy for volume in gateway-data gateway-cache; do docker run --rm -v azizam_$volume:/volume:ro -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \ tar czf /backup/$volume.tar.gz -C /volume . done The backup files hold your keys and creations. Keep them private. If you replace an installation that kept creations inside the container (an earlier version), download the creations you want to keep before the first upgrade. They are not in the new volume. Before you upgrade · Write down the current version and your deployment settings. Choose a time when few people use the gateway. Let replies and media jobs that are running finish. Stop the containers, so nothing writes to the data while you copy it. Back up both volumes and your settings. Check that you can read the backup. Upgrade a Docker Compose installation · Get the new version of the repository. Then, from the root of the repository: ShellCopy docker compose up -d --build docker compose ps Use the same settings as before. For example, set the same AZIZAM_PORT if you changed it. This command rebuilds the gateway image, including the browser interface, and can recreate the containers. Work that is running when the gateway stops is cut off. Check the result · Check the local health endpoint: ShellCopy curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:5000/health If you use a reverse proxy, check the public address too. Sign in as the owner, and check your engines and model names. On Home, select Check connection. Send a request from an app with an app key. A healthy endpoint alone does not prove that an app's engine, model and key work. Keep the backup until you have checked the new version. If a check fails, keep the logs and the backup. Do not overwrite your only copy of the old data. Restart a gateway that runs as a systemd service · If you run the gateway outside Docker, as a user systemd service, restart it with scripts/safe-restart from the root of the repository. A plain service restart can cut off streamed replies and media jobs. The script needs: Python 3, and systemctl --user with a unit for the gateway. The default unit name is azizam; change it with --unit. Node.js and npm, when the browser interface needs a rebuild. An admin key in AZIZAM_ADMIN_KEY, or in the file named by AZIZAM_ADMIN_KEY_FILE. The default key file is ~/.config/azizam/admin-key. Allow only your user to read it. A loopback --url: 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost. First, see what is running without restarting: ShellCopy scripts/safe-restart --dry-run --url http://127.0.0.1:5000 --public-url '' Then restart: ShellCopy scripts/safe-restart --url http://127.0.0.1:5000 --public-url https://gateway.example.com Replace the example public address with your own, or pass --public-url '' if the gateway has no public address. Always set it: the script's built-in default does not match your installation. The script: Builds the browser interface if it is missing or out of date. If the build fails, it stops and does not restart anything. Waits until chat has been quiet for 300 seconds. Use --quiet-seconds to change this. Drains the gateway: new POST, PUT and PATCH requests get HTTP 503 with the code gateway_draining and a Retry-After header. Reads, job checks, cancels, sign-in, administration and health checks still work. It waits for running work to finish. Restarts the service and checks local health and, if you set it, the public address. Read every warning, even when the script exits with 0. Do not use --force for a routine restart: it skips the waits and can cut off running work. Exit code Meaning 0 Restarted. Read the printed health and drain results. 1 Local health, or the public address you set, was not confirmed. 2 The command options are wrong. 3 Work was still running at the deadline. Nothing restarted. 4 The drain endpoint was unavailable or refused. Nothing restarted. 5 The service restart failed. 6 Another safe restart is running. 7 The browser interface build or publication failed. 130 Interrupted. Read the drain cleanup message.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Find where a request stopped, then take the next step for its error code.
text: Start with the error code and message in the response, not the HTTP status alone. For example, HTTP 503 can mean that the gateway is draining (gateway_draining) or that the engines are busy (resource_admission_denied). The error reference lists the codes and the next step for each. Find where the request stopped · Errors from the browser interface's routes include a layer in error.details.layer: Layer Where the request stopped request The request itself is invalid or incomplete. account Sign-in or account permissions. library A creation, file or job in Library. gateway The gateway is draining, busy or misconfigured. engine The engine cannot serve the model. model The model ran but did not produce a result. workflow The workflow's input mapping. unknown The gateway cannot tell where it stopped. The gateway does not start · Run docker compose ps and check that the containers are running. Run docker compose logs gateway and read the last lines. Check that nothing else uses the port. To use another port, see Install Azizam. An app cannot connect · Check the base URL. Do not add a second /v1 or /api. Check that the key is an app key, not an admin key or a provider key. A 127.0.0.1 address points to the device or container that sends the request. Use an address that reaches the gateway from there. A request is refused · Sign in again if the code is not_authenticated or session_user_not_found. Check the app's access plan if a model or protocol is missing. Changing the plan does not need a new key. A model is unavailable · Open Models and use a model name that your key can see. Check the engine's status. If the status is unknown, check its health settings in Connect engines. A job or restart fails · Do not assume that an interrupted job resumes. Follow the error for that job. If a safe restart reports busy, wait for the work to finish. If it reports that the drain endpoint is unavailable, check the local address and the admin key. Do not use --force. See Upgrade and back up. If local health passes but the public address fails, check the reverse proxy's route to the gateway. Ask for help · Collect the error code, the layer and a short description of the request. Remove keys, cookies, private addresses, prompts and private media first.

title: API overview
summary: Choose a protocol and base URL, authenticate with an app key, and handle errors.
text: The gateway speaks several protocols at one address. Use the protocol your app or SDK already knows. Retrieve openapi.json from your own gateway at $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/openapi.json. It describes the routes included in that gateway's OpenAPI schema. Some compatibility routes are excluded; their pages say so. Set up your environment · Run the following setup in Bash. The shell examples require curl with --fail-with-body support; JSON-encoding examples also require Python 3. Run Bash first if your current shell is different. Copy export AZIZAM_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:5000' read -r -s -p 'App key: ' AZIZAM_API_KEY; printf '\n'; export AZIZAM_API_KEY export AZIZAM_MODEL='my-chat' AZIZAM_BASE_URL is the gateway address, with no trailing slash. Use the address the owner gave you. AZIZAM_API_KEY is your app key. Do not use an admin key or a provider's key. AZIZAM_MODEL is a model name that your key can use. my-chat is an example. Find real names with the request below. Keep keys out of source control, shared logs and screenshots. Choose a base URL · Client Base URL OpenAI SDKs and apps $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/openai/v1 (/v1 also works) Anthropic SDKs $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/anthropic Ollama clients that add /api $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/ollama A1111 clients $AZIZAM_BASE_URL (routes under /sdapi/v1) MCP clients $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/mcp, with Streamable HTTP Check access and find models · ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/openai/v1/models" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" The response lists the models your key can use. Model names depend on each gateway's settings. For the gateway's own discovery, use /gateway/v1/capabilities. If a model or protocol is missing, the app's access plan may not allow it. Changing the plan does not need a new key. Handle errors · Check both the HTTP status and the appropriate protocol's error body. Do not assume every error has a field named code. Error codes lists the shapes and codes. Compatibility routes keep their protocol's error format. Status Meaning What to do 400, 422, 501 The feature or input is not supported. Check the protocol page. Do not retry unchanged. 401 The key is missing or not valid. Check the key. 413 The request is too large. See request limits. 429, 503 The gateway, an engine or a provider is busy, or the gateway is draining. Wait for Retry-After, then retry. Follow Retry-After when it is present. For a media-job submission, retry a lost response with the same idempotency key and unchanged request, subject to the replay rules in Media jobs. Do not assume that other media endpoints deduplicate retries. Protocols · OpenAI-compatible API: chat, Responses, embeddings, images, audio and video. Anthropic-compatible API: Messages. Ollama-compatible API: chat, generate and embeddings. A1111-compatible API: text to image for SD WebUI clients. Media jobs: picture work that survives a lost connection. MCP for agents: media tools for agents. Client setup examples: settings for common chat apps and editors.

title: OpenAI-compatible API
summary: Use Chat Completions, Responses and the media routes with OpenAI SDKs.
text: Set your SDK's base URL to $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/openai/v1 and its API key to your app key. /v1 also works as a base URL. The routes cover chat completions, legacy completions, embeddings, models, images, audio and video. Which models and media tasks work depends on the gateway's engines and workflows. Set the environment variables in the API overview first. Chat with curl · ShellCopy python3 - <<'PY' | curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/openai/v1/chat/completions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- import json, os print(json.dumps({"model": os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}]})) PY Add "stream": true to get the reply as a stream of events. Chat with Python · Install the openai package first. PythonCopy import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url=os.environ["AZIZAM_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/openai/v1", api_key=os.environ["AZIZAM_API_KEY"], ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model=os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}], ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) Responses · The Responses API runs through the same chat pipeline. It supports streaming, function tools, image inputs, reasoning items and structured text output. PythonCopy response = client.responses.create( model=os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], input="Say hello in one sentence.", ) print(response.output_text) You can retrieve or delete a stored response, and continue from it with previous_response_id. A stored response belongs to the app and person that created it. Any key of that app can read it. For anyone else, previous_response_id returns HTTP 404 with previous_response_not_found. Limits · Assistants, files, batches and fine-tuning are not available. Their routes return HTTP 400 with unsupported_operation. Responses does not support input_file, background, conversation, prompt, cancel or input token counting. Hosted tools are left out, and the x-azizam-omitted-tools header names them. Forcing a hosted tool returns HTTP 400. Reasoning summaries are not produced. Realtime over WebSocket needs a speech engine. Realtime over HTTP, client secrets, SIP and WebRTC are not supported. Music and sound effects at /v1/audio/generate are a gateway extension, not part of the OpenAI SDK. For picture work that should survive a lost connection, use Media jobs. For every route and field, see the gateway's OpenAPI document.

title: Anthropic-compatible API
summary: Send Messages requests with Anthropic SDKs, and know what is translated.
text: Set your SDK's base URL to $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/anthropic. The Messages route is /anthropic/v1/messages, and /v1/messages also works. Send your app key as x-api-key or as a bearer token. Set the environment variables in the API overview first. Messages with curl · ShellCopy python3 - <<'PY' | curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/anthropic/v1/messages" -H "x-api-key: $AZIZAM_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- import json, os print(json.dumps({"model": os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], "max_tokens": 256, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}]})) PY Messages with Python · Install the anthropic package first. PythonCopy import os from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic( base_url=os.environ["AZIZAM_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/anthropic", api_key=os.environ["AZIZAM_API_KEY"], ) message = client.messages.create( model=os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], max_tokens=256, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}], ) for block in message.content: if block.type == "text": print(block.text) What works · The gateway translates Messages requests into its chat pipeline. Streaming, system prompts, multi-turn history, image blocks and tool calls work, including tool results, tool choice and streamed tool arguments. Models are listed at /anthropic/v1/models. Token counting at /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens is an estimate: about four characters per token. Limits · Document blocks and server tools return HTTP 400. Web search, computer use, citations, batches and files are not supported. cache_control markers and anthropic-beta headers do not turn on prompt caching or beta features. Cache usage fields are absent. A stop sequence can stop the reply, but the response does not say which one matched. Thinking output has an empty signature. Earlier thinking blocks in the history are dropped. Errors use the Anthropic shape and include a request-id header. The request ID does not link to a gateway receipt. Status Error type 400 invalid_request_error 401 authentication_error 402 billing_error 403 permission_error 404 not_found_error 413 request_too_large 429 rate_limit_error 529 overloaded_error Other 5xx api_error These routes are in the gateway's OpenAPI document.

title: Ollama-compatible API
summary: Use Ollama clients for chat, generate and embeddings, without model file management.
text: For a client that adds /api to its base URL, use $AZIZAM_BASE_URL/ollama. For a client that always calls /api at the root of the host, use $AZIZAM_BASE_URL. Send your app key as a bearer token or as x-api-key. The gateway needs a key, unless the owner allows anonymous model discovery for tags and version. Set the environment variables in the API overview first. Chat with curl · This example turns streaming off, so the response is one JSON object. ShellCopy python3 - <<'PY' | curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/ollama/api/chat" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- import json, os print(json.dumps({"model": os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], "stream": False, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}]})) PY Chat with Python · Install the ollama package first. PythonCopy import os from ollama import Client client = Client( host=os.environ["AZIZAM_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/ollama", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["AZIZAM_API_KEY"]}, ) response = client.chat( model=os.environ["AZIZAM_MODEL"], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}], stream=False, ) print(response.message.content) What works · Chat and generate stream by default, as newline-delimited JSON. Tools, images, JSON and schema output, and thinking work. The routes also include embed, embeddings, tags, show, ps and version. Sampling options go to the engine. Read a model's details with /ollama/api/show. Limits · pull, push, create, copy, delete and blobs return HTTP 501. The gateway does not manage model files. Runtime options such as num_ctx, num_gpu and num_thread are accepted and ignored. Set them on the engine. suffix, template and raw return HTTP 400. A load or unload request with an empty prompt gets a normal response, but does not load or free a model. These routes are in the gateway's OpenAPI document. See Client setup examples for client settings.

title: A1111-compatible API
summary: Make pictures from SD WebUI clients through the gateway's image workflows.
text: Set your client's URL to the gateway address, $AZIZAM_BASE_URL. The routes are under /sdapi/v1. The gateway turns text-to-image requests into its own image workflows, and waits for the result. The model list comes from the gateway's image models and workflows. Send your app key as a bearer token or as x-api-key. For a client that uses Basic authentication, use the app key as the password. First follow Set up your environment. Run the model-list request below, then export AZIZAM_IMAGE_MODEL with an exact title from that response before running either generation example. Choose a model · ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/sdapi/v1/sd-models" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" Replace the example value with a title from the response, then run: ShellCopy export AZIZAM_IMAGE_MODEL='REPLACE_WITH_MODEL_TITLE' Text to image with curl · The response is JSON. Its images list holds base64 image data. This example saves the response to a file. ShellCopy python3 - <<'PY' | curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/sdapi/v1/txt2img" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --output txt2img.json --data-binary @- import json, os print(json.dumps({"prompt": "A blue ceramic bowl on a plain table.", "override_settings": {"sd_model_checkpoint": os.environ["AZIZAM_IMAGE_MODEL"]}})) PY Text to image with Python · This example uses only the Python standard library. It saves the first picture. PythonCopy import base64 import json import os from urllib.request import Request, urlopen body = { "prompt": "A blue ceramic bowl on a plain table.", "override_settings": {"sd_model_checkpoint": os.environ["AZIZAM_IMAGE_MODEL"]}, } request = Request( os.environ["AZIZAM_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/sdapi/v1/txt2img", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={ "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["AZIZAM_API_KEY"], "Content-Type": "application/json", }, ) with urlopen(request, timeout=660) as response: result = json.load(response) with open("picture", "wb") as f: f.write(base64.b64decode(result["images"][0])) Check the file type before you add an extension. Routes · txt2img, options, sd-models, samplers, schedulers, upscalers, latent-upscale-modes, sd-vae, progress and interrupt. A route that lists choices does not mean the gateway supports those features. The selected model is kept per app until the gateway restarts. An interrupt affects only that app's work. Limits · Hires fix, face restoration, scripts, styles, refiners, variation seeds and LoRA prompt tags return HTTP 422. img2img, extras upscaling, interrogate and png-info return HTTP 501. Settings the gateway ignores are named in the x-azizam-ignored-params header. They can include the negative prompt, sampler, scheduler, cfg_scale and clip_skip. A VAE choice is dropped. The list of VAEs is empty. Steps and guidance can be clamped to the workflow's range. An invalid size, tiling, seed resizing, an unsupported override_settings key, or more than 10 pictures in one request returns HTTP 422. A request that takes more than ten minutes returns HTTP 504. These routes are not in the gateway's OpenAPI document.

title: Media jobs
summary: Submit picture work as a job, check its progress, and download the result.
text: A job keeps working when your connection drops. Save its job_id and check the job. Do not start a new job only because a connection closed. POST /gateway/v1/media/jobs takes an intent and a request. This page uses image.generate, whose request is an OpenAI image request. The route also accepts image.edit, audio.generate, music.generate, sfx.generate and video.generate. Other intents return unsupported_media_job. Set the environment variables in the API overview first, and export AZIZAM_IMAGE_MODEL with an image model your key can use. Submit a job · Generate an idempotency key once for new work. If the submission response is lost, rerun only the submission pipeline with the same key and unchanged request. Do not rerun the key-generation line for a retry. ShellCopy export AZIZAM_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY="$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')" python3 - <<'PY' | curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/gateway/v1/media/jobs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $AZIZAM_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --output job.json --data-binary @- import json, os print(json.dumps({"intent": "image.generate", "request": {"model": os.environ["AZIZAM_IMAGE_MODEL"], "prompt": "A blue ceramic bowl on a plain table.", "n": 1}})) PY Check the job · ShellCopy JOB_ID=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("job.json"))["job_id"])') curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/gateway/v1/media/jobs/$JOB_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" Check again every few seconds. State Meaning queued, running The job is active. succeeded, failed, canceled The job is finished. Treat any other state as not finished. To cancel, send POST /gateway/v1/media/jobs/{job_id}/cancel. HTTP 202 means that the cancel was requested. Keep checking the job: it is not finished until it reaches a finished state. Read progress events · ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/gateway/v1/media/jobs/$JOB_ID/events" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" Each job numbers its events with its own sequence. Keep the highest sequence you processed for each job, so that repeated events do not update your interface twice. Do not compare sequence numbers between jobs. An event's payload holds only progress fields, such as progress, step, total, phase and status. Query parameter Meaning after_sequence Return only events after this sequence number. limit Events per page. Default 50, at most 200. To read only new events, pass the highest sequence you have as after_sequence. Retry safely · Retry a lost submission response with the same idempotency key and unchanged request. Use a new key for new work. Do not rely on a changed request replaying the old job: the media-job store rejects mismatched or unverifiable owner, operation or input with idempotency_conflict. The store retains replay eligibility while a job is active, or while its last update is within 14 days. After that, a repeated submission can start new work. Download the result · When the job has succeeded, read its content. Before that, this route returns HTTP 409 with media_job_not_ready. ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/gateway/v1/media/jobs/$JOB_ID/content" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" Job results are signed URLs, not base64 data. Anyone with a signed URL can download the file until the URL expires, without a key. Share it as carefully as a key, and do not change its query parameters. Keep the asset ID if you want to use the result as an input later. Any key of the app that created an asset can reuse it by ID. Other apps get HTTP 403. To get a fresh signed URL for an asset your app owns: ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/gateway/v1/assets/$ASSET_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" Agents can run media workflows with the MCP run and job tools.

title: MCP for agents
summary: Connect an agent to the gateway's media tools over Streamable HTTP with an app key.
text: The gateway runs an MCP server at /mcp. Connect with Streamable HTTP, and send your app key in an Authorization: Bearer header. A request without a key gets HTTP 401 with a protected-resource metadata challenge. The gateway has no OAuth server, so use a client that can send the key as a header. Tools · Tool What it does capabilities Lists the media workflows and model names you can use. Pass target to see one target's inputs. Filter with query and intent. run Starts a target with inputs. mode is auto, sync or async. For async work, wait_seconds defaults to 30, up to 120. job Reads a job by job_id, waits for it, or requests cancellation with cancel: true. Continue polling until its status is succeeded, failed or canceled. Call capabilities before you build inputs. Do not assume that an example model exists. Successful media results include signed URLs in resource_link blocks and asset records in structuredContent. Capability results and unfinished jobs do not necessarily include assets. For image and video inputs, use an asset ID, a signed asset URL from this gateway, or a data URI. The server does not fetch other URLs. Check the HTTP status and any top-level JSON-RPC error first. For a tool result, check isError and structuredContent.status. A failed or canceled job can have status failed or canceled without isError. Read its error field. Tool execution uses the existing core routes with the caller's credentials. Claude Code · With AZIZAM_BASE_URL and AZIZAM_API_KEY set: ShellCopy claude mcp add gateway "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/mcp" --transport http \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${AZIZAM_API_KEY}" The client stores the header in its configuration. Protect that file. Pi with pi-mcp-adapter · Add the server to .mcp.json. Replace the example address with your gateway's address, and keep the key in the environment: JSONCopy { "mcpServers": { "gateway": { "url": "https://gateway.example.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${AZIZAM_API_KEY}" }, "protocolVersion": "auto" } } } protocolVersion can be legacy, auto or 2026-07-28. Test with curl · This request uses the server's legacy-compatible path to list capabilities. It does not start media generation. ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/mcp" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"capabilities","arguments":{}}}' Protocol details · Protocol revisions: 2026-07-28, and the earlier 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25. The server is stateless. It issues no session IDs and has no SSE streams. GET and DELETE on /mcp return HTTP 405. For revision 2026-07-28, MCP-Protocol-Version must match params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"], Mcp-Method must match method, and Mcp-Name must match params.name for tools/call. A compatible client supplies these fields. The server offers tools only. Resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation, tasks and subscriptions are not supported. MCP is not in the gateway's OpenAPI document. Use capabilities for each target's inputs.

title: Client setup examples
summary: Connect common chat apps, editors and image tools to your gateway.

headings.text: Editors with an OpenAI Compatible provider

text: Every client needs three things: the gateway address with the right base path, an app key, and a model name that the key can use. Menus and file formats change between client versions, so treat these as examples. For most chat apps and editors, use the OpenAI-compatible base URL. Use the Anthropic or Ollama routes only when a client requires them. Check the connection first · First follow Set up your environment. Run this check on the same computer, or in the same container, as the client. ShellCopy curl --fail-with-body -sS "$AZIZAM_BASE_URL/openai/v1/models" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZIZAM_API_KEY" 127.0.0.1 reaches the computer or container that sends the request. If the gateway runs somewhere else, use its address. Open WebUI · In Settings → Connections → OpenAI: Base URL: your gateway address followed by /openai/v1 API key: your app key Refresh the model list. Model file management through Ollama panels does not work through the gateway. Picture making needs an image engine on the gateway. LibreChat · Add a custom endpoint to librechat.yaml. Replace my-chat with a model name returned by your gateway. Replace baseURL with the gateway address reachable from the LibreChat server or container, followed by /v1. Keep the loopback example only if both services share that network namespace. YAMLCopy endpoints: custom: - name: "Azizam" apiKey: "${AZIZAM_API_KEY}" baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:5000/openai/v1" models: default: ["my-chat"] fetch: true Set AZIZAM_API_KEY in LibreChat's environment. Do not write the key into the file. Features that need the OpenAI Assistants API do not work. Editors with an OpenAI Compatible provider · For editor extensions such as Cline: API provider: OpenAI Compatible Base URL: your gateway address followed by /openai/v1 API key: your app key Model ID: a chat model from the gateway's model list Tool calls use the OpenAI tool format. The model must support tool calls. Continue · Use an OpenAI provider with the /openai/v1 base URL. Choose a chat model for chat and autocomplete, and a model that supports embeddings for embeddings. One model may not do both. Set context size and other runtime options on the engine, not in the editor. SillyTavern pictures · Choose Stable Diffusion Web UI (AUTOMATIC1111) as the image source. SD WebUI URL: the gateway address, without /v1 or /sdapi/v1 Authentication: gateway: followed by your app key Connect and choose an image model. Turn off Hires fix, Restore faces and scripts. Read the A1111 limits before you turn on other settings. When setup fails · Check the base URL. Do not add a second /v1 or /api. Check that the key is an app key. Refresh the model list, and choose a name that this gateway returns. If a protocol or model is missing, ask the owner to check the app's access plan. Keep keys and signed URLs out of anything you share. For an agent, see MCP for agents.

title: People and roles
summary: How people, roles and apps fit together, and who can see whose work.
text: A person is a human account on the gateway. Azizam keeps a person separate from the apps they use and the keys those apps hold. Two main controls are roles and access plans. An active category policy can add restrictions to requests. Roles control who can administer the gateway. Access plans control which requests an app can make. See Access plans. An app key never becomes an admin key, even when the person who holds it is an administrator. Roles · Role Can administer the gateway Can see other people's Library and Usage Owner Yes Yes Superadmin Yes Yes Admin Yes No Member No No The gateway checks the stored role on every administration request. Everyone starts with their own work in Library and Usage. Only an owner or a superadmin can choose another person or everyone. The list of running jobs stays personal, for the owner too. People and automation · A personal app belongs to a person. A service app belongs to a service account. This gives an integration its own identity, without pretending to be a person. When you turn off a person's account, their personal apps stop working. When you turn off an app, it stops working. Read Apps and keys and Privacy and the owner next.

title: Apps and keys
summary: What an app is, what a key proves, and why a personal key can read saved prompts.

headings.text: A personal key can read saved prompts

text: An app is a client that uses the gateway. A key proves that a request may act as that app. An app can have more than one key, so you can replace a key without losing the app's history. Kinds of app · A personal app belongs to a person. A service app belongs to a service account. A session app is how the browser interface acts for a signed-in person. It has no key, and a key for it is not accepted. App keys and admin keys · App keys run requests. Admin keys change the gateway's configuration. Neither one can do the other's job. The gateway shows a new app key once, when it is created. It stores only a hash and a short prefix. Key lists never show the full key. Save the key somewhere safe, and never put it in a public page or a repository. A revoked or expired key is refused. A key also needs an enabled app and a valid access plan. A personal key can read saved prompts · A personal app key acts as its person only when that same person created it. Anyone who holds such a key can read that person's saved prompts. A service key, or a personal key that someone else created, does not act as a person. Prompts sent with it are not saved to anyone's prompt memory. This does not prevent an app from explicitly saving a conversation. A request to responses with store: true can save a conversation until it is explicitly deleted. Protect a personal key as you would your password. Read Prompt saving for the retention choices, and Apps & keys to create, rotate and revoke keys.

title: Access plans
summary: How an app's access plan allows or refuses each request.

headings.text: Seeing a model is not the same as running it
Trusting an address instead of a key

text: An access plan is a named set of rules that decides which requests an app may make. The API calls it a profile. A plan can limit protocols, workflows, models, engines and capabilities. It also sets rules for remote providers, fallback, status visibility and whether a request may start a model that is not loaded. Which plan applies · For a request with an app key, the gateway uses the first of these that is set: The plan set on the key. The app's default plan. For an app that belongs to a person, that person's plan. If the person has no plan, the default plan for their role or sign-in group. The built-in default plan. If the selected plan is missing or invalid, the request is refused. A turned-off app cannot run requests. You can change an app's default plan without issuing new keys. A key with its own plan keeps using that plan instead. How a request is checked · The gateway checks the rules in order. The first refusal wins. For protocol, workflow, model and engine allow-lists, an unset list adds no restriction. An empty list refuses requests that supply that value. Capability selectors apply only when the request supplies the corresponding metadata. Remote providers must be explicitly allowed. Native passthrough must be enabled separately. Its empty engine and operation lists add no restriction. Capability rules use the labels that describe each model. A label is not proof of what a model or its output contains. Cloud fallback and paid fallback are separate permissions. Allowing a provider does not, by itself, allow paid fallback. Seeing a model is not the same as running it · A plan can show every configured model, or only the models available now. It can also allow or refuse starting a model that is not loaded. Seeing a model in the list does not mean that it is loaded. Categories can add more restrictions to a request that a plan allows. They cannot allow a request that the plan refuses. Trusting an address instead of a key · By default a request with no key is refused. An owner can change that for one device, or one network, without giving up the access plan. Open Apps & keys, choose the app, and add a trusted address. Enter one IP address or a range such as 192.168.1.0/24. A request with no key that comes straight from that address runs as that app. The app's access plan limits it, and each request shows the app and the address. No address is trusted until an owner adds one. A key that is sent always decides the request, even from a trusted address. Only the address of the direct connection counts. The gateway reads X-Forwarded-For only when the connection comes from a reverse proxy listed in auth.trusted_proxies. A request that shows signs of an unlisted proxy never matches. Turn the app off, or remove the address, and the address stops working at once.

title: Categories
summary: How category rules add restrictions on top of access plans.

headings.text: If the rules cannot be read

text: Category enforcement has not been verified for this release. Do not rely on the coverage, revision-matching or failure behavior described below as a security guarantee. Categories let the owner describe policy in their own words, as data. For example, an owner could create a category for a group of people and say which models it may use. That is an example, not a built-in rule. The category check runs after the access plan allows a request. It can only make the decision stricter. It never allows a request that the plan refused. When category rules apply · With no active category policy, categories add no restrictions. A request is governed when its person or its app is listed in the active policy. People and apps that are not listed keep the access plan's decision. A governed request needs a category plan that covers both its person and its app, and an entry for the requested workflow or model. Missing coverage refuses the request. How a model is matched · A policy entry names a model or workflow with a revision, for example example-model@review-1. It matches requests for example-model. That name is an example, not an installed model. If the rules cannot be read · If the active policy cannot be read or is invalid, the gateway refuses every request that the access plan allowed, with POLICY_UNAVAILABLE. It never ignores the policy. Category labels are policy that the owner writes. They do not inspect or guarantee what a model produces.

title: Engines and models
summary: Why the engines and models you can use depend on each gateway's settings.

headings.text: Configured is not the same as running

text: Every gateway has its own engines, so there is no fixed list of models for Azizam. Each gateway's catalog shows what that gateway offers. Engine, model and workflow · An engine record describes a server that does model work: its address, health probe, priority and capabilities. A model name is the name apps use. The owner maps it to the engine's own model ID. A workflow is a named task, with the inputs it needs. A workflow runs on an engine. For example, an owner could connect one engine for chat and another for pictures. That is an example of settings, not a promise that either engine exists on your gateway. Settings, not code · The owner can add, change, turn off and remove engine records. The gateway records each change in its activity history. You can change engine records without editing gateway code. A replacement still needs to support a protocol and capabilities that the gateway can use. Configured is not the same as running · A model in the catalog is not always loaded. An access plan decides whether an app sees all configured models or only the ones available now, and whether a request may start a model that is not loaded. To add or change an engine, see Connect engines.

title: Providers and spend
summary: How permission to use a paid provider works, and why recorded spend is not a bill.

headings.text: Recorded spend is not a bill

text: A provider is a remote service that the gateway can send requests to. Most providers charge for use. Permission to use a provider · Each access plan has a list of allowed providers. A request for a provider that is not on the list is refused. Paid fallback is a separate permission. Allowing a provider does not allow the gateway to fall back to it when a local engine is unavailable. A local model that is down does not become a paid request unless you set that up. Spend settings · An access plan can hold a per-request limit, a daily budget and a monthly budget, in US dollars. All apps on the plan share its budgets. The daily budget covers the last 24 hours. The monthly budget covers the calendar month. Before a paid request, the gateway estimates its cost and reserves it against the budgets. It refuses the request if the reservation would go over a limit. After the request, it records the actual cost. Requests that are already running can take spend past a budget. When a budget is set, the gateway refuses paid requests whose cost it cannot estimate. A charge that is not yet reconciled blocks further paid requests. Set a spending limit with the provider too. Recorded spend is not a bill · Usage adds up the costs recorded in receipts. Some requests have no recorded cost. Usage shows how many requests have a measured cost, and how many paid requests have an unknown cost. A total of zero with no measured requests does not prove that nothing was spent. Use the provider's billing records to check what it actually charged. See Receipts and usage.

title: Receipts and usage
summary: What a receipt records, and how Usage counts requests and spend.
text: A receipt records what happened to one request. When an access plan decides a request, the receipt can also hold the decision and its reasons. Usage builds its summary from receipts and from the records of creations. Receipts do not hold prompts or workflow graphs. Those are kept separately; see Prompt saving. The current month · Usage covers the current calendar month. The month starts at midnight UTC on the first day. Totals count every kept top-level receipt in the month. The list of recent requests shows up to 50. That limit does not change the totals. Usage shows requests, failures, creations, activity by day and activity by model. Whose activity you see · You see your own activity by default. An owner or a superadmin can choose another person or everyone. The gateway records each time someone views everyone's activity. Usage says whether the month is complete. If earlier history is not available, the month is marked partial. Costs · Spend counts only the costs recorded in receipts. Usage shows how many requests have a measured cost and how many paid requests have an unknown cost. A missing cost does not mean free. The provider's bill can include charges that are not shown here. See Providers and spend.

title: Library and retention
summary: What the gateway keeps, for how long, and what deleting a creation does.
text: Library shows the pictures, videos and audio made through the gateway. It builds each entry from jobs, files, receipts and app ownership. An entry can show its model, workflow, time, size, source and how long it took, when those facts were recorded. An entry can stay in the list after its file is gone. An entry is not a backup of its file. What the gateway keeps · Retention periods and download-link expiry have not been verified for this release. Keep your own backups and confirm the instance's retention settings before relying on stored history. Data How long Creations, jobs, job events and saved conversations No automatic time limit. Receipts No time limit by default. The owner can set a limit, with a preview of what will be deleted. Saved prompts Depends on prompt settings. See Prompt saving. Signed download links Expire. The file stays. A saved prompt can expire or be erased without deleting the creation. What deleting a creation does · Deleting from Library works only on your own creations, for the owner too. It removes your saved prompt for that creation and records the deletion. The gateway tries to delete the stored file. It keeps the file if its metadata lists more than one ownership key or more than one maker. Multiple keys can belong to the same app. Removing a creation from your Library does not always erase the stored file or other copies. Retention settings are not a backup plan. Disk space, engines and backups need their own care. See Upgrade and back up.

title: Privacy and the owner
summary: What other people on the gateway can see, and what the owner can always read.

headings.text: The operator can read the storage

text: The gateway keeps creations and saved prompts under separate access rules. These rules control the application. They do not hide anything from the person who runs the computer. What other people see · Library and Usage start with your own work. Members cannot see other people's work. An admin role alone does not show other people's Library. An owner or a superadmin can see other people's creations and usage. The gateway records requests to the everyone Library and Usage views, and requests for download links from the everyone Library view. The list of running jobs stays personal, for the owner too. Saved prompts · Library shows a saved prompt only to the person who made the creation. When the owner opens someone else's creation, they do not see its prompt. Download with details includes the saved prompt and workflow. Only the person with that saved prompt can download it. A personal app key can read its owner's saved prompts only when that same person created the key. A personal key created by someone else does not act as that person. Protect an owner-created personal key as you would your password. See Apps and keys. The operator can read the storage · Saved prompts are stored in the gateway's database. Anyone with direct access to that storage can read them. Self-hosting does not hide your data from the person who runs the gateway. Use a gateway run by someone you trust. Prompt settings control what the gateway keeps. They do not control copies kept by an engine, a provider or a backup.

title: Prompt saving
summary: How long prompts are kept, and what a one-request "don't keep" choice does.
text: The gateway can keep the prompt for a picture, speech or workflow request, separate from the creation. It can also keep the workflow details, for a full download that only the maker can get. By default, prompts are kept with no time limit. Each person can turn keeping off. The owner can set the default, set a shorter limit, or turn keeping off for everyone. Don't keep one prompt · In Try, turn on Don’t keep this prompt. See Try. From the API, add this object to the request body: JSONCopy { "extensions": { "com.azizam.prompts": { "mode": "forget" } } } Keep the other fields the endpoint needs. The only accepted value is "mode": "forget". A request cannot force a prompt to be kept when the person or the owner has turned keeping off. A Responses API request with store: false is also treated as "don't keep". How long prompts are kept · Setting Stored value No time limit never (never expires) 90 days 3_months 365 days 1_year When a person's choice and the owner's limit are both set, the shorter one wins. Expired prompts are not shown. Limits · Not keeping a prompt does not delete the creation, and does not hide the request from Usage. Keeping a job's input does not guarantee that it will resume after a restart. An interrupted job can fail without being rerun. Check Library before making the item again. The choice does not control what an engine or a provider keeps. Service keys never save prompts for a person. See Apps and keys.

title: Configuration
summary: Settings for the listener, setup, request limits, media downloads and monitoring.
text: The gateway reads its settings from a configuration file and from environment variables. An environment variable overrides the matching field in the file. Most settings take effect when the gateway starts. Relative paths in the configuration file resolve from the gateway's working directory. In the Docker image, that is the root of the repository. Do not write secret values into the configuration file. Settings that need a secret take the name of an environment variable instead, for example api_key_env: NAME. Listener and network · Variable Default Effect AZIZAM_PORT 5000 The port the gateway listens on. In Docker Compose, the host port. AZIZAM_DOCKER_SUBNET 172.30.251.0/24 The Compose network's subnet. AZIZAM_DOCKER_GATEWAY 172.30.251.1 The Compose network's gateway address. Change it together with the subnet. AZIZAM_SETUP_ALLOWED_CIDRS none; Docker Compose sets it to the Compose gateway address Networks that may create the owner account. Overrides auth.setup_allowed_cidrs. Loopback is always allowed. Request limits · Variable Configuration field Default AZIZAM_REQUEST_BODY_JSON_BYTES request_body_limits.json_bytes 33,554,432 bytes (32 MiB) AZIZAM_REQUEST_BODY_MEDIA_BYTES request_body_limits.media_bytes 537,919,488 bytes (513 MiB) Values must be positive byte counts. Changes take effect when the gateway starts. The media limit applies to image, audio, video, face, media job, workflow and /sdapi/v1 routes, and to the media routes under /openai/v1.
